description: CodeBuild project service roles must include both the s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation permissions for any S3 bucket associated with the project.

decisionPoints.description: Whether the build project is associated with an S3 bucket at all, and through which association (build output artifacts, source, secondary artifacts, secondary source, cache, or build log storage)
Whether the service role the project runs under can be tied to a role definition present in the same template, or is only referenced as an external identity
Whether the permission set granted to the project's service role includes the S3 get-bucket-ACL permission
Whether the permission set granted to the project's service role includes the S3 get-bucket-location permission

How the grant is expressed — exact action names, wildcard action patterns, letter casing, allow versus deny effect, and whether the two permissions are spread across multiple statements or multiple policy documents attached to the same role
Which S3 resources the granting statement applies to relative to the bucket associated with the project
Whether the role reference, the granted actions, or the bucket identity is only determined at deployment time and cannot be resolved during analysis

requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket and has no other S3 bucket associated with it, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy allowing both the get-bucket-ACL and get-bucket-location permissions on that bucket, with no statement denying either of those permissions on that bucket
requirements.rationale: With the artifacts bucket as the project's only S3 association and an in-template role policy that allows both get-bucket-ACL and get-bucket-location on that bucket with nothing denying them, the role's effective permissions are exactly the two the CodeBuild guidance requires.
requirements.evidence: Searched CodeBuild IAM documentation: "Secure access to S3 buckets" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/auth-and-access-control-iam-access-control-identity-based.html) states the service role must itself carry s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation for the S3 bucket associated with the project, since these are not in AWS managed policies. Searched IAM policy evaluation logic: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic_policy-eval-denyallow.html — "An explicit deny overrides an explicit allow"; the enforcement code first scans all applicable policies for a Deny and returns Deny if any applies. Applying that answer, an Allow for both actions on the artifacts bucket yields the effective permissions the CodeBuild doc requires only when nothing explicitly denies them. As originally written this description also covered a policy carrying an additional explicit Deny on GetBucketAcl (REQ-23's case), which the premise says does not effectively hold the permission; the description is therefore narrowed to exclude any denying statement on those permissions for that bucket, leaving the pass verdict correct for the remaining scope.

requirements.description: Project takes its build source from an S3 bucket and produces no build output, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy allowing both the get-bucket-ACL and get-bucket-location permissions on that bucket
requirements.rationale: The only S3 bucket associated with the project is the S3 source bucket (artifacts are NO_ARTIFACTS), and the in-template service role's policy already grants both s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation on that bucket, which is exactly what CodeBuild documents as required for secure access to project S3 buckets.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on which S3 buckets count as "associated with the project" here and whether the co-located role grants both required actions on them. Searched AWS docs for "CodeBuild service role policy s3:GetBucketAcl s3:GetBucketLocation" and for CodeBuild S3 source bucket permissions. The CodeBuild User Guide, "Overview of managing access permissions to your AWS CodeBuild resources" (section "Secure access to S3 buckets"), states: "We strongly recommend that you include the following permissions in your IAM role to verify the S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project is owned by you or someone you trust. These permissions are not included in AWS managed policies and roles. You must add them yourself: s3:GetBucketAcl, s3:GetBucketLocation." The related troubleshooting page confirms these are the two actions CodeBuild calls for bucket-ownership verification. In this configuration the project's source type is S3 and it produces no build output, so the source bucket is the only associated S3 bucket; no artifact or cache bucket exists to require additional coverage. The service role is defined in the same template, so its policy is resolvable at analysis time, and that policy allows both s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation on that bucket. The documented requirement is therefore fully satisfied and the rule has nothing to report.

requirements.description: Project uses an S3-backed build cache with no other S3 association, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy allowing both the get-bucket-ACL and get-bucket-location permissions on the cache bucket
requirements.rationale: The project's only S3 association is its S3 build cache bucket, and the in-template service role already grants both s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation on that bucket, which is exactly the pair of permissions the rule requires.
requirements.evidence:
What the verdict turns on: whether the service role attached to the CodeBuild project carries s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation for every S3 bucket the project is associated with — here, only the S3-backed build cache bucket.

Searched the AWS docs for "CodeBuild service role policy s3:GetBucketAcl s3:GetBucketLocation" and "CodeBuild cache S3 bucket permissions service role". The CodeBuild "Overview of managing access permissions" page, section "Secure access to S3 buckets," states: "We strongly recommend that you include the following permissions in your IAM role to verify the S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project is owned by you or someone you trust. These permissions are not included in AWS managed policies and roles. You must add them yourself: s3:GetBucketAcl, s3:GetBucketLocation." This confirms (a) the permissions are the bucket-ownership-verification protection the rule enforces, (b) they are never supplied by default or by an AWS managed policy, so they must appear explicitly — and (c) the scope is "the S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project," which for this configuration is the cache bucket and nothing else. The CodeBuild troubleshooting page corroborates the same pair as the ownership check ("Error calling GetBucketAcl: Either the bucket owner has changed or the service role no longer has permission to called s3:GetBucketAcl").

No absent-value/default question arises: the deciding facts are all present in the template. The role is defined in the same template (so the scanner can resolve it), it is the role the project runs under, and its policy allows both actions on the cache bucket — the sole S3 association. The documented requirement is therefore satisfied in full, and the resource as deployed will run with the ownership-verification permissions in place. Nothing is deferred to deployment time, so no intrinsic exception applies. Flagging here would produce a finding a reviewer would dismiss.

requirements.description: Project writes build logs to an S3 bucket with log delivery enabled and has no other S3 association, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy allowing both the get-bucket-ACL and get-bucket-location permissions on the log bucket
requirements.rationale: The only S3 bucket associated with the project is the build-log bucket, and the in-template service role's policy already grants both s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation on that bucket, so the permission pair the rule demands is fully present.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether every S3 bucket the project is associated with is covered by both s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation in the service role. Here the sole association is the S3 LogsConfig log-delivery bucket (S3Logs status ENABLED with a location), and the role, defined in the same template, grants both actions on that bucket — so nothing is missing and no absent value needs a service default looked up. I searched the AWS docs for "CodeBuild service role s3:GetBucketAcl s3:GetBucketLocation S3 build logs" and for the S3 logs configuration permissions. The CodeBuild troubleshooting page (docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/troubleshooting.html) confirms that s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation on the project's S3 bucket are exactly the pair used to secure the project's bucket ("Secure access to S3 buckets"), which is the pair the rule requires. The S3LogsConfig API reference (bucketOwnerAccess, encryptionDisabled, location, status) shows the log bucket is an S3 association of the project and notes only that bucketOwnerAccess additionally needs s3:PutBucketAcl — a separate permission this rule does not cover, and bucketOwnerAccess defaults to NONE so it is not implicated. No other implicit S3 association (artifacts, cache, source) exists in this configuration for which the permissions could be missing. The configuration therefore satisfies the rule as documented and no finding is owed.

requirements.description: Project produces no primary build output but declares an additional output artifact stored in an S3 bucket, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy allowing both the get-bucket-ACL and get-bucket-location permissions on that bucket
requirements.rationale: The only S3 bucket associated with this project is the one holding its secondary (additional) output artifact, and the in-template service role already grants both s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation on that bucket, so the permissions the rule demands are present.
requirements.evidence:
What the verdict turns on: whether the rule's required pair of permissions is present for every S3 bucket "associated with the project," given that the primary artifacts entry produces no output (NO_ARTIFACTS) and the only S3 bucket in play comes from a secondary/additional artifact declaration, plus whether the role being defined in the same template lets the scanner resolve it.

Searches performed: (1) "CodeBuild service role s3:GetBucketAcl s3:GetBucketLocation policy", (2) "CodeBuild secondaryArtifacts S3 artifacts type NO_ARTIFACTS", (3) "CodeBuild secure access to S3 buckets GetBucketAcl GetBucketLocation service role artifacts".

What the docs said: the CodeBuild access-control overview, section "Secure access to S3 buckets" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/auth-and-access-control-iam-access-control-identity-based.html), states: "We strongly recommend that you include the following permissions in your IAM role to verify the S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project is owned by you or someone you trust. These permissions are not included in AWS managed policies and roles. You must add them yourself: s3:GetBucketAcl, s3:GetBucketLocation." This is the exact source of the rule and it is scoped to any S3 bucket associated with the project, not just the primary artifact bucket. The CodeBuild create-project reference confirms secondaryArtifacts is an array of ProjectArtifacts objects using "many of the same settings used by the artifacts object" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/create-project.html), so a secondary S3 artifact bucket is genuinely an associated bucket that the service role writes to — it is in scope for the rule even though the primary artifacts type yields no output. The troubleshooting page ("Error calling GetBucketAcl...") corroborates that these permissions are the ones CodeBuild exercises against the project's bucket.

Why it decides pass: the in-scope bucket here is the secondary artifact bucket, and the service role — defined in the same template, so its policy is resolvable at analysis time — allows both s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation on that bucket. Both required actions are covered for the only associated bucket, so the documented recommendation the rule encodes is satisfied and there is nothing for the rule to report. No default-value question arises: the permissions are explicitly present, and the absence of a primary output does not create an unprotected bucket (a NO_ARTIFACTS primary contributes no bucket at all).

requirements.description: Project takes its primary source from a git hosting provider and declares an additional source located in an S3 bucket, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy allowing both the get-bucket-ACL and get-bucket-location permissions on that bucket
requirements.rationale: The S3 bucket backing the project's secondary source is covered by an in-template service-role policy that already allows both s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation, which is exactly the pair CodeBuild requires for buckets associated with a project, so there is nothing left for the rule to require.
requirements.evidence: What the verdict turns on: whether the two required actions are present on the S3 bucket that the project associates with itself, and whether a secondary (additional) source bucket counts as "associated with the project". Searched AWS docs for "CodeBuild service role s3:GetBucketAcl s3:GetBucketLocation", "CodeBuild secondary sources S3 bucket permissions service role", and "CodeBuild secure access to S3 buckets". The CodeBuild User Guide, "Overview of managing access permissions to your AWS CodeBuild resources" → "Secure access to S3 buckets", states: "We strongly recommend that you include the following permissions in your IAM role to verify the S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project is owned by you or someone you trust. These permissions are not included in AWS managed policies and roles. You must add them yourself." and lists exactly s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation. The scope is any "S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project" — the guide draws no distinction between primary and secondary sources, so an S3 secondary source bucket is in scope even though the primary source is a git provider. The related troubleshooting page ("Error calling GetBucketAcl…") confirms these are the operations CodeBuild actually invokes against such a bucket at build time. In this configuration the service role is defined in the same template and carries a policy allowing both the get-bucket-ACL and get-bucket-location actions on that same bucket, so the deployed state already matches the documented requirement. No default or absent value is in play — the permissions are affirmatively granted — so the rule has nothing to report. Note the git-hosted primary source contributes no S3 bucket of its own; the only associated bucket is the secondary source, and it is covered.

requirements.description: Project takes its source from a git hosting provider, produces no build output, uses no cache, and sends logs only to a log group service, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy that grants neither the get-bucket-ACL nor the get-bucket-location permission
requirements.rationale: The rule only requires s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation for S3 buckets associated with the project, and this project associates none — a git-provider source, NO_ARTIFACTS output, no cache (the service default is NO_CACHE), and logs sent only to CloudWatch Logs — so the role's lack of those two actions cannot leave any project bucket unverified.
requirements.evidence:
Searched CodeBuild IAM docs for "s3:GetBucketAcl s3:GetBucketLocation". The authoritative statement is in "Overview of managing access permissions to your AWS CodeBuild resources" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/auth-and-access-control-iam-access-control-identity-based.html), section "Secure access to S3 buckets": AWS recommends including s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation in the IAM role "to verify the S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project is owned by you or someone you trust"; the purpose is bucket-ownership verification, and the troubleshooting page (Error calling GetBucketAcl...) confirms these permissions exist to guard a project's S3 bucket against ownership change. The requirement is therefore scoped to buckets the project actually uses.

Then checked which project properties can associate an S3 bucket. Per the CodeBuild artifacts type reference (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/api/v2/docs/aws-cdk-lib.aws_codebuild.CfnProject.ArtifactsProperty.html and the Kotlin SDK ArtifactsType page), NO_ARTIFACTS means "the build project does not produce any build output" — no output bucket, in contrast to type S3 which "stores build output in Amazon S3". The source comes from a git hosting provider, not S3. Cache is unused; when Cache is omitted CodeBuild applies type NO_CACHE, so no cache bucket exists either. Logs go only to a log group service (CloudWatch Logs) rather than S3Logs, so no logging bucket.

With no source bucket, no artifact bucket, no cache bucket and no logs bucket, there is no "S3 bucket associated with the project" for the two permissions to protect. The service role's policy omitting s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation leaves no bucket unverified at runtime, so the resource ends up in a state the rule accepts and the rule owes no finding. Nothing here depends on a deployment-time value; the decision comes from the documented meaning of the permissions and of NO_ARTIFACTS/NO_CACHE.

requirements.description: Project has an S3 build-log destination configured but log delivery to it is switched off, has no other S3 association, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy that grants neither the get-bucket-ACL nor the get-bucket-location permission
requirements.rationale: With the S3 logs configuration's Status set to DISABLED, CodeBuild does not write build logs to that bucket, so the project has no S3 bucket association whose ownership the service role would need s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation to verify.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether an S3 log destination whose delivery is switched off still counts as "an S3 bucket associated with the project." Searched the CodeBuild CloudFormation reference for AWS::CodeBuild::Project S3LogsConfig: the Status property is required and takes only ENABLED or DISABLED, where "ENABLED: S3 build logs are enabled for this build project" and "DISABLED: S3 build logs are not enabled for this build project" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-codebuild-project-s3logsconfig.md; same wording in the API/SDK references). Status is not an omitted value here — it is explicitly DISABLED, so no default lookup is needed: the service will not deliver logs to the named Location, and the Location string alone causes no S3 access by the service role. Searched for the rationale behind the two permissions: the CodeBuild identity-based access control page ("Secure access to S3 buckets") states the permissions s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation are recommended "to verify the S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project is owned by you or someone you trust," and the troubleshooting page shows the failure mode is a build-time GetBucketAcl call against a bucket CodeBuild actually uses. With log delivery disabled and no other S3 association (no S3 artifacts, S3 source, or S3 cache stated), there is no bucket CodeBuild will touch, so the absence of both permissions in the in-template role policy creates no exposure and no build failure. The role and its policy are defined in the same template, so the grant is fully resolvable at analysis time — this is a merits decision, not an unknown-value exception.

requirements.description: Project's build output and source are both managed by the continuous delivery pipeline service rather than named buckets, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy that grants neither the get-bucket-ACL nor the get-bucket-location permission
requirements.rationale: A project whose source and artifacts are of type CODEPIPELINE still reads and writes the pipeline's S3 artifact bucket under its own service role, so an S3 bucket is associated with the project, and the in-template role's policy grants neither s3:GetBucketAcl nor s3:GetBucketLocation.
requirements.evidence:
Searched CodeBuild IAM docs for "CodeBuild service role policy s3:GetBucketAcl s3:GetBucketLocation" and for how a CODEPIPELINE-type project accesses buckets. The CodeBuild "Overview of managing access permissions" page (Secure access to S3 buckets) states: "We strongly recommend that you include the following permissions in your IAM role to verify the S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project is owned by you or someone you trust. These permissions are not included in AWS managed policies and roles. You must add them yourself: s3:GetBucketAcl, s3:GetBucketLocation." The troubleshooting page confirms CodeBuild actually calls GetBucketAcl against the project's bucket at build time.

The deciding question is whether Source/Artifacts of type CODEPIPELINE means no S3 bucket is associated. It does not: with CodePipeline integration, input artifacts are downloaded from and output artifacts uploaded to the pipeline's S3 artifact store, and the CodeBuild build performs those S3 operations with the CodeBuild project's service role (per "Use AWS CodeBuild with AWS CodePipeline", where the CodeBuild service role must be able to access the pipeline artifact bucket; the CodePipeline access-denied guidance likewise shows s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation scoped to the pipeline artifact bucket ARN). So a bucket is associated with the project even though no bucket name appears in the project resource — the omission of an explicit S3 location does not remove the requirement, and there is no service default that supplies these permissions (the docs explicitly say they are absent from AWS managed policies and must be added manually).

The role is defined in the same template and its policy is fully readable at analysis time — no deployment-time unknown — and it grants neither permission. Therefore the rule's condition is breached and a finding is owed.

requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket and runs under a role identified only by an identifier of a role that is not defined anywhere in the template
requirements.rationale: The project writes artifacts to S3 under a service role whose policies are nowhere in the template, and AWS states that s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation are never granted by AWS managed policies or default service roles and must be added explicitly, so nothing grants them here and the required bucket-ownership verification permissions are absent.
requirements.evidence:
Searched CodeBuild IAM documentation for the two permissions ("CodeBuild service role policy s3:GetBucketAcl s3:GetBucketLocation artifacts bucket") and the CloudFormation ServiceRole property. The CodeBuild "Overview of managing access permissions to your AWS CodeBuild resources" page, section "Secure access to S3 buckets", states: "We strongly recommend that you include the following permissions in your IAM role to verify the S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project is owned by you or someone you trust. These permissions are not included in AWS managed policies and roles. You must add them yourself. s3:GetBucketAcl / s3:GetBucketLocation." The CodeBuild troubleshooting page corroborates that these are opt-in permissions the customer adds. So there is no service-applied default that supplies them: an absent grant means the permissions are absent, and the resource runs without the bucket-ownership check the rule requires.

On the deployment-time-unknown exception: the ServiceRole here is a fixed identifier of a role that simply is not declared in the template, not a value produced by a parameter or other input resolved at deploy time. The value itself is fully known; what is missing is the role's policy document, which is merely outside the scanned material. That is an absent/unreadable configuration, not an intrinsic unknown, so the exception does not apply. Combined with the documented fact that no default grants these actions, the project stores artifacts in S3 with no demonstrated s3:GetBucketAcl or s3:GetBucketLocation permission, which is exactly the condition the rule targets.

requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy allowing the get-bucket-ACL permission and object read and write permissions, but not the get-bucket-location permission
requirements.rationale: The role's inline policy grants s3:GetBucketAcl plus object read/write but omits s3:GetBucketLocation, and CodeBuild applies no implicit grant for that action — it must be added to the service role explicitly — so the deployed role is missing one of the two required bucket-ownership verification permissions.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether s3:GetBucketLocation can be satisfied by anything other than an explicit statement in the service role's policy. Searched the AWS docs for "CodeBuild service role policy s3:GetBucketAcl s3:GetBucketLocation" and for the artifacts-bucket permission requirements. The CodeBuild "Overview of managing access permissions to your AWS CodeBuild resources" page (Secure access to S3 buckets) states: "We strongly recommend that you include the following permissions in your IAM role to verify the S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project is owned by you or someone you trust. These permissions are not included in AWS managed policies and roles. You must add them yourself" — listing both s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation. So there is no default, no managed-policy fallback, and no service-applied grant: IAM is deny-by-default and an action absent from the policy is simply not permitted. The CodeBuild troubleshooting page corroborates that both actions are the pair that secures the project's bucket ("Error calling GetBucketAcl: Either the bucket owner has changed or the service role no longer has permission to called s3:GetBucketAcl ... You added the s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation permissions to your IAM role"). Here the role is defined in the same template and its policy is fully readable at analysis time — nothing is deferred to deployment — and it grants GetBucketAcl and object-level read/write only. Object-level actions (GetObject/PutObject) do not confer bucket-level GetBucketLocation. The rule requires both permissions for the associated artifacts bucket; one is missing, so the rule owes a finding.

requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy allowing the get-bucket-location permission and object read and write permissions, but not the get-bucket-ACL permission
requirements.rationale: The project's S3 artifact bucket is accessed by a service role whose policy grants s3:GetBucketLocation and object read/write but never s3:GetBucketAcl, and no service default supplies that action — IAM grants nothing that is not explicitly allowed — so the bucket-ownership verification the rule requires is absent.
requirements.evidence: Searched the AWS docs for the CodeBuild service-role S3 permission requirements ("CodeBuild service role policy s3:GetBucketAcl s3:GetBucketLocation" and "CodeBuild artifacts S3 bucket permissions GetBucketAcl required"). The CodeBuild access-control overview states: "We strongly recommend that you include the following permissions in your IAM role to verify the S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project is owned by you or someone you trust. These permissions are not included in AWS managed policies and roles. You must add them yourself" — listing s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/auth-and-access-control-iam-access-control-identity-based.html). The service-role setup page shows both actions together in an "S3BucketIdentity" statement (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/setting-up-service-role.html), and the troubleshooting page confirms CodeBuild actually calls GetBucketAcl at build time ("Error calling GetBucketAcl: ... the service role no longer has permission to called s3:GetBucketAcl"). Here the role is defined in the same template and its policy grants s3:GetBucketLocation plus object-level get/put, but omits s3:GetBucketAcl. IAM is deny-by-default and the docs explicitly say these permissions are not supplied by any managed policy or service default, so the omission is not filled in at deployment; the deciding value is fully known in the template. The rule demands both actions for any S3 bucket associated with the project, and only one is present.

requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy allowing only object-level read and write permissions on that bucket
requirements.rationale: The in-template service role grants only object-level actions (e.g. s3:GetObject/s3:PutObject on bucket/*), and IAM grants nothing implicitly — the bucket-level s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation actions the rule requires are absent and are documented as not being supplied by any AWS managed policy or default, so the deployed role will genuinely lack them.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on (a) whether the required actions can be present by some default even though the template's policy only lists object-level actions, and (b) whether object-level permissions imply the bucket-level ones. Searched AWS docs for "CodeBuild service role policy s3:GetBucketAcl s3:GetBucketLocation artifacts" and "CodeBuild S3 artifacts bucket permissions required". The CodeBuild Identity-Based Policies page ("Secure access to S3 buckets", https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/auth-and-access-control-iam-access-control-identity-based.html) states: "We strongly recommend that you include the following permissions in your IAM role to verify the S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project is owned by you or someone you trust. These permissions are not included in AWS managed policies and roles. You must add them yourself: s3:GetBucketAcl, s3:GetBucketLocation." That settles the default question: there is no default or managed-policy source for these actions — if the template's policy does not list them, the role does not have them. IAM is deny-by-default and bucket-level actions (GetBucketAcl, GetBucketLocation) are distinct from object-level actions and are evaluated against the bucket ARN, not arn:...:bucket/*, so a policy allowing only object read/write cannot confer them; CodeBuild's own sample policies (e.g. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/sample-fastlane.html) show the bucket-level statement separately from the object-level statement. The role here is defined in the same template, so its permissions are fully visible at analysis time — nothing is deferred to deployment. The CodeBuild troubleshooting page further confirms these permissions are actively used by builds against the project's S3 bucket. Configuration therefore breaches the rule.

requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a trust relationship only and no permission policies of any kind attached or embedded
requirements.rationale: The project's S3 artifact bucket requires the service role to grant s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation, and a role defined with only a trust policy and no attached or inline permission policies grants no S3 actions at all — IAM roles have no implicit permissions, so neither action is present.
requirements.evidence: Searched AWS docs for "CodeBuild service role policy s3:GetBucketAcl s3:GetBucketLocation" and for the permissions required for CodeBuild S3 output artifacts. The CodeBuild User Guide, "Overview of managing access permissions to your AWS CodeBuild resources" (Secure access to S3 buckets), states: "We strongly recommend that you include the following permissions in your IAM role to verify the S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project is owned by you or someone you trust. These permissions are not included in AWS managed policies and roles. You must add them yourself: s3:GetBucketAcl, s3:GetBucketLocation." The troubleshooting page confirms CodeBuild actually calls GetBucketAcl against the project bucket. This configuration associates an S3 bucket with the project (output artifacts), so the rule applies. The role in the template has only an AssumeRolePolicyDocument — no ManagedPolicyArns, no Policies (inline), no separate AWS::IAM::Policy/ManagedPolicy attaching to it. IAM grants nothing by default: a role with only a trust relationship can assume-be-assumed but authorizes no actions, and the docs explicitly say the two actions are not supplied by managed policies either. There is no deployment-time-unknown value here — the absence of any permission policy is fully determinable at analysis time, and no possible value could supply the permissions. Therefore both required permissions are definitively absent and the rule owes a finding.

requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a single policy document in which one statement allows the get-bucket-ACL permission and a separate statement allows the get-bucket-location permission on that bucket
requirements.rationale: Both required permissions are granted on the project's artifact bucket, and IAM unions Allow statements within a policy document, so splitting s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation across two statements yields the same effective permissions as listing them together.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on (a) whether these two permissions are the ones CodeBuild requires for a project's associated S3 bucket, and (b) whether granting them in two separate statements of the same policy document is equivalent to granting them in one. Searched the CodeBuild IAM access-control docs: "Overview of managing access permissions to your AWS CodeBuild resources" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/auth-and-access-control-iam-access-control-identity-based.html) states under "Secure access to S3 buckets" that AWS strongly recommends including s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation in the IAM role to verify the S3 bucket associated with the CodeBuild project is owned by you, and that these are not in AWS managed policies so they must be added manually — confirming both actions are exactly what the rule demands, and the artifact bucket is an associated bucket. Searched IAM policy evaluation semantics: "Policies and permissions in AWS IAM" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html) says you can define more than one permission for a role using multiple statements in a single policy, even recommends breaking policies up by resource type, and that "Regardless of the combination of multiple statements and multiple policies, AWS evaluates your policies the same way." requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket, and the role it runs under has the get-bucket-ACL permission granted through a policy embedded in the role while the get-bucket-location permission is granted through a separately declared policy document associated with the same role

Here the project does use an S3 bucket (build output artifacts), so the rule is in scope, and both required actions are granted to that role — one inline, one via a separate attached policy document. requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy document that contains no permission statements

requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy whose only allowed action is a wildcard matching every action of the S3 service on that bucket

API actions, use the * wildcard as follows: \"savingsplans:*\"". requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy whose only allowed action is a wildcard pattern covering all S3 actions whose names begin with the get verb, scoped to that bucket

requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with one statement allowing both the get-bucket-ACL and get-bucket-location permissions on that bucket and a further statement denying the get-bucket-ACL permission on the same bucket

requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy allowing both the get-bucket-ACL and get-bucket-location permissions scoped only to the objects inside that bucket rather than to the bucket itself

The managed-policies page confirms the CodeBuild AWS managed policies (AWSCodeBuildAdminAccess/DeveloperAccess/ReadOnlyAccess, plus AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess for artifacts) are the service-provided set, and none is documented as carrying these bucket-ownership verification actions. So the opacity of the managed policy in the template is not an analysis-time unknown: AWS documentation resolves its contents with respect to these two actions — they are absent by definition. The project stores artifacts in an S3 bucket, so a bucket is associated with the project and the requirement applies. With no inline or customer-managed policy granting the actions, the deployed role will run without them, which breaches the rule. This is not the intrinsic-exception case (no deployment-time-resolved input decides it) and not a strict-default fallback, since documentation settles it directly.

requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy allowing both the get-bucket-ACL and get-bucket-location permissions on a wildcard resource pattern that, rather than naming the bucket exactly, matches the associated bucket's identifier by prefix in a way that still covers the bucket resource itself and not only the objects within it
requirements.rationale: A wildcard resource pattern that still matches the plain bucket ARN of the associated bucket grants the bucket-level get-bucket-ACL and get-bucket-location operations, which is what the rule requires; naming the bucket exactly is not necessary.
requirements.evidence: Same sources: the S3 'How Amazon S3 works with IAM' page requires the Resource element for bucket operations to identify the bucket-type ARN (arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name), and IAM policy resource elements support wildcards, so a pattern such as arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket* matches that bucket ARN and effectively grants s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket. The CodeBuild 'Secure access to S3 buckets' guidance only requires that the role hold these two permissions for the project's bucket; it does not require the ARN to be written literally. The shared overlap case (arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/*) is a prefix-matching wildcard that nonetheless never matches the bucket ARN, so the description has been narrowed to wildcard patterns that do cover the bucket resource itself, leaving object-only scoping to REQ-26.

requirements.description: Project is associated with two different S3 buckets, one holding build output artifacts and another used as the build cache, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy allowing both the get-bucket-ACL and get-bucket-location permissions scoped only to the artifacts bucket
requirements.rationale: The S3 build cache bucket is an S3 bucket associated with the project and CodeBuild accesses it under the service role, yet the ownership-verification permissions are granted only for the artifacts bucket, leaving the cache bucket uncovered.
requirements.evidence: The same CodeBuild guidance (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/auth-and-access-control-iam-access-control-identity-based.html) recommends s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation for the S3 bucket associated with the project so its ownership can be verified, without narrowing that to artifacts, and warns these permissions are absent from AWS managed policies. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/caching-s3.html confirms an S3 cache bucket is a project-level S3 location that CodeBuild automatically stores and updates under the project's service role, i.e. a bucket associated with the project. Here the policy is scoped only to the artifacts bucket, so the cache bucket gets no ownership-verification permissions and is not covered; there is also no service default that supplies IAM permissions, and the troubleshooting page (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/troubleshooting.html) shows CodeBuild actually calls GetBucketAcl at build time. The description already isolates this case exactly, so no restatement is needed.

requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket, and the role it runs under is defined in the same template with a policy where the get-bucket-ACL permission is named exactly and the get-bucket-location permission is covered only by a wildcard action pattern, both scoped to that bucket
requirements.rationale: A wildcard action pattern that matches s3:GetBucketLocation grants that permission just as an exact action name does, so the role scoped to the project's artifact bucket effectively holds both s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation.
requirements.evidence:
What the verdict turns on: whether a wildcard action pattern (e.g. "s3:GetBucket*" or "s3:*") in the service role's policy satisfies the rule's requirement for s3:GetBucketLocation, given s3:GetBucketAcl is named literally and both are scoped to the project's S3 artifact bucket.

Searches performed:
1. "CodeBuild service role policy s3:GetBucketAcl s3:GetBucketLocation" — the CodeBuild "Overview of managing access permissions to your AWS CodeBuild resources" page (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/auth-and-access-control-iam-access-control-identity-based.html) confirms the rule's substance: "We strongly recommend that you include the following permissions in your IAM role to verify the S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project is owned by you or someone you trust... s3:GetBucketAcl, s3:GetBucketLocation. These permissions are not included in AWS managed policies and roles. You must add them yourself." The CodeBuild troubleshooting page corroborates that the pair is what secures the project's S3 bucket. Neither page requires the permissions to be spelled out literally — the requirement is on the permission being granted.
2. IAM Action-element wildcard semantics — AWS IAM documentation states that multiple actions may be specified with wildcards and that such a pattern covers every matching API action, e.g. "You can also specify multiple actions using wildcards. For example, you can specify all Savings Plans API actions whose name begins with the word 'Describe' as follows: \"Action\": \"savingsplans:Describe*\"" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/identity-access-management.html), the same Action-element grammar that applies to s3: actions.

Why this decides pass: the rule is about the effective permissions of the deployed service role, not the literal strings in the template. IAM policy evaluation expands a wildcard action pattern to every action it matches, so a pattern that covers s3:GetBucketLocation grants s3:GetBucketLocation with the same effect as naming it. With s3:GetBucketAcl named exactly, a wildcard covering the get-bucket-location action, and both statements scoped to the bucket the project writes artifacts to, the role the project runs under holds both required permissions on that bucket. Nothing is unresolved at analysis time — the role and its policy are defined in the same template, so the scanner can see the grant. The rule owes this configuration no finding.

requirements.description: Project stores build output artifacts in an S3 bucket and names its service role by a literal role identifier string that corresponds to a role definition also present in the same template, which allows both the get-bucket-ACL and get-bucket-location permissions on that bucket
requirements.rationale: The project's service role is resolvable in-template by its literal role identifier and its policy already allows both s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation on the artifact bucket, which is exactly the pair of permissions the rule requires.
requirements.evidence:
What the verdict turns on: whether the service role attached to the CodeBuild project actually carries both s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:GetBucketLocation for the S3 bucket the project uses for artifacts, and whether the scanner can resolve that role at analysis time.

Searched AWS docs for "CodeBuild service role s3:GetBucketAcl s3:GetBucketLocation permissions" and "CodeBuild project artifacts S3 bucket service role policy required permissions". The CodeBuild User Guide, "Overview of managing access permissions to your AWS CodeBuild resources" (section "Secure access to S3 buckets"), states: "We strongly recommend that you include the following permissions in your IAM role to verify the S3 bucket associated with your CodeBuild project is owned by you or someone you trust. These permissions are not included in AWS managed policies and roles. You must add them yourself: s3:GetBucketAcl, s3:GetBucketLocation." The troubleshooting page ("Error calling GetBucketAcl...") confirms these are the two permissions that secure the project's S3 bucket. So the rule's requirement is precisely this documented pair, and there is no service-applied default that grants them — they must appear explicitly in the role.

Applied to this configuration: the project stores output artifacts in an S3 bucket and its ServiceRole is a literal role identifier string matching a role defined in the same template, so the role is fully resolvable at analysis time (no deployment-time unknown). That role's policy allows both the get-bucket-ACL and get-bucket-location actions on that bucket. The end state of the deployed resource therefore satisfies the documented recommendation in full: both required actions are present for the associated bucket. Nothing is left to a default, and no permission is missing, so the rule has nothing to report.
